$comment: VERSIONED CONTENT, NOT CODE (hard rule 14; the precedent is content/assignor-relationships.json and CLAUDE.md §7 'option lists are content'). Every field pattern AOBPRINTER uses to turn a printed DB4 into a DB4 Print Record lives here, and `version` travels on every record produced from it as `parserTemplateVersion` — so a record can always be re-read against the template that made it. A practice management system changes its print layout without asking us; when PracSoft does, this file is copied to a new version and the old one keeps explaining the records it produced. NOTHING HERE ASSERTS THE FORM'S VALIDITY OR ITS VERSION: the driver says 'DB4, as printed' and the server decides whether that is the post-1-July form (DB4-AND-AOBL.md §1d, §2). A FIELD THAT DOES NOT MATCH IS ABSENT FROM THE RECORD, never defaulted and never guessed. CALIBRATED AGAINST A PROBE, NOT AGAINST PRACSOFT: the fixture at test-fixtures/pracsoft3-db4-probe.pdf was printed to AOBPRINTER on this machine on 17 September 2026 from a plain-text page laid out like the scanned DB4. It proves the mechanism end to end; it is NOT PracSoft's real output, and the first real print from the practice will need these patterns checked line by line and this file bumped to a new version. SUPERSEDES pracsoft3-db4-2026-09-1 (D-2026-10-10-08): identical to it in every extractor except the service rows, where `benefitAssigned` now keeps the amount exactly as printed, `$` and grouping commas included. The -09-1 file is unchanged and stays built in, so the records it stamped can still be re-read against it.
$comment_constants: Facts about the form itself rather than about one printing of it. `formCode` is what the page IS, not a claim that it is current. `currency` is on the form's own amounts. `statementsJoinedBy` is the word printed between the two assignment statements.

extractors.$comment: The four heading lines as printed, in order (Carl, 14 Sep 2026). A heading may WRAP across two printed lines, so each entry is started by its own pattern and absorbs the lines after it until the next start or the stop.
formReference is the correlation key for every later message about this form, and the filename the Signed-DB4 goes back as (§6a).

True only when the printed page already carries a signature the driver can SEE in the text layer. An ink signature is pixels and is invisible here, so this is a marker PracSoft prints, not a detection. A boolean whose pattern is declared and does not match is false — we looked and it was not there — which is a determination, not a guess. THE MARKER TEXT IS UNCONFIRMED against real PracSoft output; check it on the first real print.
The service date printed on the first service row. Read from the page rather than derived from the rows, so the record says what the form says.
The street lines between the practice name and the patient block. The suburb/state/postcode line is excluded here because it is captured as its own three fields below.

The practice's own chart number. It is the join key everywhere — the patient folder the Signed-DB4 goes back into, and the only identifier used to match a patient. The Medicare number below is never used for that (hard rule 1, D-2026-09-14-03).

CARRIED, NEVER AN IDENTIFIER. D-2026-09-14-03: the Medicare card number and IRN are printed on the form and travel on the record, because the Signed-DB4 reproduces the form and the auditor links the form to the claim by that number. Hard rule 1 is unchanged: the number is never used to verify who somebody is, never used to find or match a patient, never in a log line, an error message, a filename or an event, and never sent to the rules service.

Given names are everything before the last whitespace-separated token, which is how PracSoft prints a patient line. A single-token name yields a family name and no given names rather than a guess at which it is.
Two providers, two roles, and we model one of them as the servicing provider (§1e). The provider number is the practice's own key, so `pmsProviderKey` is derived from it.

The service rows, in printed order. `benefitAssigned` is the amount PracSoft printed, AS PRINTED: the `$` and any grouping comma are inside the captured group, and `collapseSpaces` only trims it and folds a run of spaces to one (Carl, 10 Oct 2026, D-2026-10-10-08: a real DB4 prints `$45.05`, and the patient should see `$45.05`). It is a string from here to the Signed-DB4; nothing parses it to a number, and AoB never originates or computes one (hard rule 4 as narrowed by D-2026-09-14-02). The -09-1 template applied `money` here and produced `45.05`.

The privacy notice as printed, one entry per paragraph, so it can become versioned render content later rather than being hardcoded into a template (Carl: 'in case we need to make these dynamic in the future').
startPatterns: ^To be completed by the person assigning

extractors.$comment: Statement one — the assignment this product is about. `ticked` is what the driver could see on the page.
extractors.pattern: ^(?<tick>\[[ Xx]?\])?\s*(?<text>I assign my right to benefits.*?)\s*$

extractors.$comment: Statement two is a PATHOLOGY assignment — s 65C(4) items 1-4, out of this product's scope (CLAUDE.md §8). It is carried as data and never acted on: never validated, never rendered for a patient to tick, never written back. `inScope: false` is what says so on the record.
extractors.pattern: ^(?<tick>\[[ Xx]?\])?\s*(?<text>I offer to assign my right to benefits.*?)\s*$

extractors.$comment: Referral particulars. None of these is on a plain bulk-bill attendance, and all of them are absent from the record when the form does not print them — which is the rule: absent, never guessed.
